contracts.name: Achilles and the Tortoise
contracts.statement: Finite distance is traversed in finite steps using geometric series summation.
contracts.formal_proposition: Linear kinematic intersection d_meet = v_A * t = d0 + v_T * t refutes the assertion that Achilles never catches the tortoise.
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-001: Achilles and the Tortoise
(declare-const d0 Real)
(declare-const vA Real)
(declare-const vT Real)
(declare-const t Real)
(assert (= d0 9.0))
(assert (= vA 10.0))
(assert (= vT 1.0))
(assert (> t 0.0))
(assert (= (* vA t) (+ d0 (* vT t))))
; Refuting hypothesis that Achilles distance is strictly less than tortoise distance
(assert (< (* vA t) (+ d0 (* vT t))))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Russell Set Paradox
contracts.statement: Set of all sets that do not contain themselves creates ungrounded self-reference.
contracts.formal_proposition: Unrestricted comprehension R = {x | x not in x} yields R in R <=> not(R in R), which is logically refutable.
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-002: Russell Set Paradox
(declare-const in_R Bool)
(assert (= in_R (not in_R)))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Barber Paradox
contracts.statement: Barber shaves all and only those who do not shave themselves.
contracts.formal_proposition: In a first-order relational structure, forall x (shaves(b, x) <=> not(shaves(x, x))) is first-order unsatisfiable.
assumptions: Barber is a member of the domain
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-003: Barber Paradox
(declare-sort Person)
(declare-fun shaves (Person Person) Bool)
(declare-const barber Person)
(assert (forall ((x Person)) (= (shaves barber x) (not (shaves x x)))))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Liar Paradox
contracts.statement: Sentence asserting its own falsehood ("This statement is false").
contracts.formal_proposition: A proposition asserting T <=> not(T) is unsatisfiable in classical bivalent truth systems.
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-004: Liar Paradox
(declare-const truth_value Bool)
(assert (= truth_value (not truth_value)))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Grelling-Nelson Paradox
contracts.statement: Is "heterological" (a word not describing itself) heterological?
contracts.formal_proposition: Semantic predicate Het(w) <=> not(Applies(w, w)) applied reflexively to Het yields Het <=> not(Het), refutable in bivalent semantics.
assumptions: Words can be predicates over words
constraints: applies is a 2-place relation on words
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-005: Grelling-Nelson Paradox
(declare-sort Word)
(declare-fun applies (Word Word) Bool)
(declare-const het Word)
(assert (forall ((w Word)) (= (applies het w) (not (applies w w)))))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Curry Paradox
contracts.statement: Self-referential conditional implies arbitrary falsehood without negation.
contracts.formal_proposition: Sentence C asserting C => F allows proving arbitrary falsehood F via contraction (modus ponens with self-premise).
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-006: Curry Paradox
(declare-const C Bool)
(declare-const arbitrary_falsehood Bool)
(assert (= C (=> C arbitrary_falsehood)))
(assert (not arbitrary_falsehood))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Berry Paradox
contracts.statement: The smallest positive integer not definable in under eleven words.
contracts.formal_proposition: Kolmogorov complexity bound: Integer N having complexity K(N) >= L cannot have description length < L.
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-007: Berry Paradox
(declare-const L Int)
(declare-const KN Int)
(declare-const desc_len Int)
(assert (> L 100))
(assert (>= KN L))
(assert (<= desc_len 50))
(assert (>= KN desc_len))
(assert (< KN desc_len))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Richard Paradox
contracts.statement: Diagonalization over all definable real numbers.
contracts.formal_proposition: If all definable reals in (0, 1) are enumerated, diagonal element r differs at the n-th position from the n-th definable real. Claiming r is in the enumeration is refutable.
assumptions: Diagonal construction differs at every index
constraints: k is a valid enumeration index
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-008: Richard Paradox
(declare-const r_is_in_enumeration Bool)
(declare-const r_differs_at_index_k Bool)
(assert (=> r_is_in_enumeration (not r_differs_at_index_k)))
(assert r_is_in_enumeration)
(assert r_differs_at_index_k)
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Burali-Forti Paradox
contracts.statement: The ordinal number of all ordinals must be greater than itself.
contracts.formal_proposition: Strict well-ordering on ordinals is irreflexive (not alpha < alpha). Supposing the class of all ordinals is a set with ordinal Omega forces Omega < Omega, refuting sethood.
assumptions: Ordinals are well-ordered by strict membership
Every set of ordinals has an upper bound ordinal
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-009: Burali-Forti Paradox
(declare-const Omega_ord Int)
(assert (< Omega_ord Omega_ord))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Cantor Paradox
contracts.statement: Power set of universal set must have strictly greater cardinality than universal set.
contracts.formal_proposition: For universal set U, |P(U)| <= |U|. Cantor theorem proves |U| < |P(U)|. The conjunction is refutable.
assumptions: Power set operation is valid on U
axioms: Subsets of universal set belong to universal set
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-010: Cantor Paradox
(declare-const cardU Int)
(declare-const cardPU Int)
(assert (> cardU 0))
(assert (> cardPU cardU))
(assert (<= cardPU cardU))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Sorites Paradox
contracts.statement: Removing one grain from a heap leaves a heap; by induction one grain is a heap.
contracts.formal_proposition: Crisp induction on bounded tolerance boundary (heap(n) => heap(n-1)) forces heap(1) from heap(5), refuting the negative boundary condition.
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-011: Sorites Paradox
(declare-fun is_heap (Int) Bool)
(assert (is_heap 5))
(assert (not (is_heap 1)))
(assert (forall ((n Int)) (=> (and (>= n 2) (<= n 5) (is_heap n)) (is_heap (- n 1)))))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Ship of Theseus
contracts.statement: Gradual replacement of every part raises persistent identity ambiguity.
contracts.formal_proposition: Identity transitivity requires that if continuous ship A = B and reconstructed ship A = C, then B = C. Asserting B != C refutes classical equivalence.
assumptions: Original material reassembly preserves identity (A = C)
constraints: A, B, C are distinct token states
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-012: Ship of Theseus
(declare-sort Ship)
(declare-const shipA Ship)
(declare-const shipB Ship)
(declare-const shipC Ship)
(assert (= shipA shipB))
(assert (= shipA shipC))
(assert (not (= shipB shipC)))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Grandfather Paradox
contracts.statement: Time traveler prevents own lineage, invalidating the travel premise.
contracts.formal_proposition: Lineage consistency: Time travel T requires traveler birth B (T => B). Travel execution action causes not(B) (T => not B). Asserting T yields contradiction B and not B.
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-013: Grandfather Paradox
(declare-const traveler_born Bool)
(declare-const travel_occurred Bool)
(assert (=> travel_occurred traveler_born))
(assert (=> travel_occurred (not traveler_born)))
(assert travel_occurred)
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Bootstrap Paradox
contracts.statement: An object or information is sent back in time, creating uncaused existence.
contracts.formal_proposition: Classical strict causal orders are irreflexive (not causes(x, x)). An uncaused ontological time-loop asserting causes(e, e) is refutable.
assumptions: Causality is a strict partial order
Ontological loop event e causes itself
axioms: Irreflexivity and transitivity of strict causality
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-014: Bootstrap Paradox
(declare-sort Event)
(declare-fun causes (Event Event) Bool)
(assert (forall ((x Event)) (not (causes x x))))
(assert (forall ((x Event) (y Event) (z Event)) (=> (and (causes x y) (causes y z)) (causes x z))))
(declare-const e Event)
(assert (causes e e))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Raven Paradox (Hempel)
contracts.statement: Observing a green apple confirms "All ravens are black" via contrapositive.
contracts.formal_proposition: Universal implication (forall x: Raven(x) => Black(x)) is logically equivalent to its contrapositive (forall x: not Black(x) => not Raven(x)). Non-equivalence is refutable.
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-015: Raven Paradox (Hempel)
(declare-sort Entity)
(declare-fun is_raven (Entity) Bool)
(declare-fun is_black (Entity) Bool)
(declare-const hyp1 Bool)
(declare-const hyp2 Bool)
(assert (= hyp1 (forall ((x Entity)) (=> (is_raven x) (is_black x)))))
(assert (= hyp2 (forall ((x Entity)) (=> (not (is_black x)) (not (is_raven x))))))
(assert (not (= hyp1 hyp2)))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Goodman New Riddle of Induction (Grue)
contracts.statement: Predicate "grue" (green before t, blue after) equally supported by evidence.
contracts.formal_proposition: Simultaneous projection of color predicates: At future time t_future, an object cannot be simultaneously green and blue under mutually exclusive color categories.
assumptions: Green and Blue are disjoint color predicates
Grue definition shifts at time threshold t
axioms: Mutual exclusivity of fundamental color terms
constraints: is_green and is_blue cannot both be true
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-016: Goodman New Riddle of Induction (Grue)
(declare-const is_green Bool)
(declare-const is_blue Bool)
(assert (not (and is_green is_blue)))
(assert is_green)
(assert is_blue)
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Newcomb Problem
contracts.statement: Superintelligent predictor: choose One Box ($1M) or Two Boxes ($1M + $1K).
contracts.formal_proposition: Dominance principle dictates choosing two boxes while Expected Utility under perfect prediction dictates choosing one box. Simultaneous single-choice satisfaction is refutable.
assumptions: Expected utility under perfect predictor: choose one box
axioms: Exclusive decision choice between one and two boxes
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-017: Newcomb Problem
(declare-const choose_one_box Bool)
(declare-const dominance_recommends_two Bool)
(declare-const eu_recommends_one Bool)
(assert (= dominance_recommends_two (not choose_one_box)))
(assert (= eu_recommends_one choose_one_box))
(assert dominance_recommends_two)
(assert eu_recommends_one)
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Prisoner Dilemma
contracts.statement: Dominant individual strategy leads to suboptimal collective outcome.
contracts.formal_proposition: Strict dominance equilibrium (Defect, Defect) with payoff 1 strictly less than mutual cooperation payoff 3. Refuting that Nash equilibrium is Pareto optimal.
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-018: Prisoner Dilemma
(declare-const u_nash Int)
(declare-const u_coop Int)
(assert (= u_nash 1))
(assert (= u_coop 3))
; Refuting hypothesis that Nash payoff equals or exceeds cooperative payoff
(assert (>= u_nash u_coop))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Simpson Paradox
contracts.statement: Trend appears in groups but reverses when groups are aggregated.
contracts.formal_proposition: Subgroup success rate reversal upon aggregation: a1 > b1 and a2 > b2 while totalA < totalB is mathematically SATISFIABLE.
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-019: Simpson Paradox
(declare-const a1 Real)
(declare-const b1 Real)
(declare-const a2 Real)
(declare-const b2 Real)
(declare-const totalA Real)
(declare-const totalB Real)
(assert (> a1 b1))
(assert (> a2 b2))
(assert (< totalA totalB))
; Satisfying assignment exists: e.g., A1=80%, B1=70%, A2=20%, B2=10%, TotalA=50%, TotalB=55%
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Monty Hall Problem
contracts.statement: Switching doors doubles win probability from 1/3 to 2/3.
contracts.formal_proposition: Conditional probability update: P(win | stay) = 1/3 while P(win | switch) = 2/3. Refuting the intuitive claim that switching and staying have equal 1/2 probability.
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-020: Monty Hall Problem
(declare-const p_stay Real)
(declare-const p_switch Real)
(assert (= p_stay (/ 1.0 3.0)))
(assert (= p_switch (- 1.0 p_stay)))
; Refuting hypothesis that p_stay == p_switch
(assert (= p_stay p_switch))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Birthday Paradox
contracts.statement: In 23 people, >50% chance of a shared birthday.
contracts.formal_proposition: Combinatorial collision product: For n=23 and days=365, complementary probability Q(23) <= 0.493, yielding P(collision) > 0.5. Refuting P(collision) <= 0.5.
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-021: Birthday Paradox
(declare-const q23 Real)
(declare-const p_collision Real)
(assert (<= q23 0.493))
(assert (= p_collision (- 1.0 q23)))
(assert (<= p_collision 0.5))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Banach-Tarski Paradox
contracts.statement: A solid ball can be decomposed into 5 non-measurable sets and reassembled into two.
contracts.formal_proposition: Under finite additivity of Lebesgue measure, measurable decomposition of volume V preserves total volume V. Reassembly into 2V is refutable for measurable subsets.
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-022: Banach-Tarski Paradox
(declare-const V Real)
(declare-const sum_pieces Real)
(assert (> V 0.0))
(assert (= sum_pieces V))
; Refuting hypothesis that measurable pieces reassemble into volume 2V
(assert (= sum_pieces (* 2.0 V)))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Gabriel Horn (Torricelli Trumpet)
contracts.statement: Surface of revolution has infinite surface area but finite volume (pi).
contracts.formal_proposition: Volume integral V = pi * int_1^inf (1/x^2) dx = pi is finite, whereas surface area integral A >= 2pi * int_1^inf (1/x) dx diverges. Conjunction of finite volume with bounded surface area is refutable.
assumptions: Solid of revolution for y = 1/x on [1, inf)
axioms: Divergence of harmonic integral for p=1
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-023: Gabriel Horn (Torricelli Trumpet)
(declare-const V Real)
(declare-const A_finite Bool)
(declare-const M Real)
(assert (= V 3.14159265))
(assert (> V 0.0))
(assert (<= (* 6.28 100.0) M))
(assert (> (* 6.28 100.0) M))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Olbers Paradox
contracts.statement: In an infinite static universe, the night sky should be uniformly bright.
contracts.formal_proposition: In infinite static Euclidean space with uniform star number density, integrated flux diverges. Conjunction of infinite static universe with finite sky flux is refutable.
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-024: Olbers Paradox
(declare-const flux_finite Bool)
(declare-const static_infinite_universe Bool)
(assert static_infinite_universe)
(assert (=> static_infinite_universe (not flux_finite)))
(assert flux_finite)
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Fermi Paradox
contracts.statement: High probability of extraterrestrial life vs total absence of observational contact.
contracts.formal_proposition: Drake expectation N >> 1 with unhindered interstellar colonization implies observed civilizations > 0. The conjunction of high expected colonization with observed = 0 is refutable.
assumptions: Drake equation parameters yield large N
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-025: Fermi Paradox
(declare-const N Int)
(declare-const observed_civilizations Int)
(assert (> N 1000))
(assert (=> (> N 0) (> observed_civilizations 0)))
(assert (= observed_civilizations 0))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Twin Paradox
contracts.statement: Traveling twin accelerates away and returns younger than stationary twin.
contracts.formal_proposition: Asymmetric Minkowski spacetime proper time: tau_traveler = T * sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2) < T. Refuting hypothesis that traveling twin elapsed proper time equals stationary twin.
assumptions: Minkowski metric interval ds^2 = c^2 dt^2 - dx^2
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-026: Twin Paradox
(declare-const T Real)
(declare-const tau_traveler Real)
(declare-const v Real)
(assert (> T 0.0))
(assert (= v 0.8))
(assert (= tau_traveler (* T 0.6)))
; Refuting hypothesis that elapsed proper time is identical
(assert (= tau_traveler T))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: EPR Paradox
contracts.statement: Entangled particles exhibit instantaneous correlations ("spooky action at a distance").
contracts.formal_proposition: Bell CHSH theorem: Local hidden variable realism bounds correlation |S| <= 2. Quantum entangled state yields S = 2*sqrt(2) approx 2.828. Quantum correlation violating classical bound is refutable under local realism.
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-027: EPR Paradox
(declare-const S_quantum Real)
(declare-const S_local_hidden_bound Real)
(assert (= S_local_hidden_bound 2.0))
(assert (= S_quantum 2.8284))
; Refuting that quantum correlation satisfies classical Bell bound
(assert (<= S_quantum S_local_hidden_bound))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Schrodinger Cat Paradox
contracts.statement: Quantum superposition entangled with macroscopic feline life state.
contracts.formal_proposition: Decoherence through environment-induced superselection forces macroscopic interference terms to 0. Macroscopic persistent interference (> 0.1) is refutable.
assumptions: Macroscopic pointer state entanglement with environment
Trace over unobserved degrees of freedom
axioms: Decoherence theorem in open quantum systems
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-028: Schrodinger Cat Paradox
(declare-const p_alive Real)
(declare-const p_dead Real)
(declare-const interference_term Real)
(assert (= p_alive 0.5))
(assert (= p_dead 0.5))
(assert (= interference_term 0.0))
; Refuting non-zero macroscopic interference
(assert (> interference_term 0.1))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Zeno Arrow Paradox
contracts.statement: At every instant of time, a flying arrow occupies a space equal to itself and is motionless.
contracts.formal_proposition: Instantaneous velocity is defined as the limit dx/dt as dt -> 0. Non-zero velocity v0 > 0 refutes the claim that instantaneous occupancy implies zero velocity.
assumptions: Arrow has position trajectory x(t) = v0 * t with v0 > 0
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-029: Zeno Arrow Paradox
(declare-const v0 Real)
(declare-const v_instant Real)
(assert (> v0 0.0))
(assert (= v_instant v0))
; Refuting that arrow velocity is zero at instant t
(assert (= v_instant 0.0))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Zeno Dichotomy Paradox
contracts.statement: Motion can never start because one must traverse infinite half-intervals first.
contracts.formal_proposition: Sum of geometric intervals sum_{n=1}^inf (1/2^n) = 1 converges in finite time t0. Refuting that traversing infinite half-intervals diverges.
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-030: Zeno Dichotomy Paradox
(declare-const total_dist Real)
(declare-const total_time Real)
(declare-const t0 Real)
(assert (> t0 0.0))
(assert (= total_dist 1.0))
(assert (= total_time t0))
; Refuting that traversal time diverges
(assert (> total_time (* 2.0 t0)))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Braess Paradox
contracts.statement: Adding a road to a congested traffic network can increase overall travel times.
contracts.formal_proposition: In a congested network with non-cooperative routing, adding a shortcut edge creates a new user equilibrium with higher latency. This phenomenon is SATISFIABLE.
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-031: Braess Paradox
(declare-const latency_before Real)
(declare-const latency_after Real)
(assert (= latency_before 1.5))
(assert (= latency_after 2.0))
(assert (> latency_after latency_before))
(check-sat)

contracts.name: Byzantine Generals Paradox
contracts.statement: Reaching consensus across unreliable networks with traitorous nodes.
contracts.formal_proposition: Lamport-Shostak-Pease Theorem: Synchronous Byzantine agreement with m traitorous nodes requires strictly > 3m nodes (n >= 3m + 1). For n=3 and m=1, reaching consensus is refutable.
assumptions: Oral message model without digital signatures
contracts.z3_smt_assertion:
; DH-P-032: Byzantine Generals Paradox
(declare-const n Int)
(declare-const m Int)
(assert (= n 3))
(assert (= m 1))
; Refuting that n=3 satisfies the Byzantine tolerance threshold n >= 3m + 1
(assert (>= n (+ (* 3 m) 1)))
(check-sat)
